title: Start with a strategy. The platform does the learning. Here is the whole thing in 2 minutes
author: andrew363601
selftext:
every trading bot or strategy has the same flaw  
it trades the same way forever  
win or lose it learns nothing so I built one that does - thoughts?   
I wanted to create a platform stupid simple to use 

for beginners here is how simple it is to start...



**1 - pick a strategy**

the library has prebuilt ones. trend. chop fade. or ask the agent to write one in chat based of any indicator



**2 - backtest it**

one click. it tests the strategy PER market structure  
trend gets tested on trend days. chop on chop days  
you see exactly where it wins and where it dies  
and the test writes the playbook

https://preview.redd.it/gf2vymw5mbvh1.png?width=641&format=png&auto=webp&s=24dc2be16643f713f99d276a3b48387fb1df3f59

basically what this means - what wins in trend becomes the trend playbook   
what survives chop becomes the chop playbook - make sense?  
each market structure gets its own exits learned from the data so its not one global guess stretched over every market   
  
then it locks paramaters  
every entry is tagged with its regime at the moment it fires   
and that regime's exits ride with the trade for its whole life   
if the market flips mid trade then the trade just keeps its plan   
no guessing at exit time. the backtest already decided   
  
the agent reads this playbook before every entry   
plus the learned priors from every past run of the strategy AND IF you give it permission:

https://preview.redd.it/c0anv26ombvh1.png?width=543&format=png&auto=webp&s=34d114f88b49c89519e13621f1f29a6bf47cfef0

  
it can fine tune the geometry per trade inside bounds you set.   
every change stamped and visible

the results are real. the closes are verified against the actual exchange fill



**3 - deploy it to paper - test - then go live right away**

one button. you press deploy and now it trades a 5k paper account with real market data





**4 - the guardrails come on with it**

every entry passes risk checks first  
position size capped. leverage capped. stop loss mandatory  
risk more than the profile allows and the trade gets BLOCKED. with a message that says exactly why and the agent can also refuse a trade too - a shadow portfolio takes the simulated trade  
it reads the walls. the flow. its own memory of what failed/worked last time  
if the setup smells wrong it vetoes and writes down why  
then it sits in a cooldown so it cannot revenge trade  
and on every open trade a tripwire locks your capital at break even  
a traill follows price so a winner is always harvesting alpha 

https://preview.redd.it/t5yehktwkbvh1.png?width=594&format=png&auto=webp&s=3d7990a2e815e6139fa848466e41d880e2ab148b

  
**5 - the loop starts**

every trade ends with an autopsy  
another agent grades the reasoning. not the money  
a good thesis can loose, and bad one can get lucky  
the grade becomes a lesson with a tag on it  
the week the loop ran clean it printed 183 closed trades on paper!  
watch the learning loop chart on the dashboard. predicted vs realized  
when those two lines meet the agent is honest

https://preview.redd.it/kqnj1wd4lbvh1.png?width=994&format=png&auto=webp&s=9dc25c8ca830d3438399de670d97130daa2015fa

and here is the part that is hard to copy: (IMO)  
last week the agent watched both walls on a falling market migrate up it wrote its own instruction into memory. verbatim

***"IF both cage legs re-base up by twenty cents with a demand bank confirmed below THEN enter only as a bank anchored buy limit at the deepest floor plus five cents"***

with the take profit parked right in front of the biggest ask wall  
it set its own entry - its own levels - its own take profit  
then it closed the trade verified against the exchange fill  
and graded its own reasoning in the autopsy  
the lesson scored 197 stays in memory forever  
that is NOT a chatbot reading a signal  
that is a PERSISTENT agent deriving its own trade geometry from live order book math  
and teaching itself the next version of the entry, which is just INSANE!!!

  
**6 - the platform gets smarter while you sleep**

every 6 hours the trainer retrains  
72 models right now. one per asset per regime per strategy  
your closed trades are the data that builds them  
the models publish their own win rates on the dashboard  
the model announces when it is bad

https://preview.redd.it/ze8ob8gwmbvh1.png?width=960&format=png&auto=webp&s=340365a5567278b65e60468d37847ba8221c0abd

  
**7 - the next trade is smarter**

the agent checks its memories before every entry  
has this pattern failed recently? the lessons will so  
small buckets get shrunk so they cannot pretend to know things  
and if it keeps making the same mistake it gets told in plain text  
and yes the pnl is real. every close is verified against the exchange fill  
real price. real fees. no invented exits...

https://preview.redd.it/vn8m4lyxmbvh1.png?width=732&format=png&auto=webp&s=d22b26fb9291dc82b3e8e467fe923a1a2e04d216



**the 100k challenge is live - back right now**

5k paper account. real exchange feed  
max 10x leverage. max 25% per position  
5 trades min to rank. 

public leaderboard is here - starting is free: [nexustradingagent.com/leaderboard](http://nexustradingagent.com/leaderboard)

  
a stratagys code can be copied in an afternoon  
  
the loop grading itself in public for months cannot - thats the moat

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: testing trend strategies only on trend days has one trap: you only know it was a trend day after the close. if the label for a day uses that same day's bars, the backtest is grading itself with the answer key. how does it decide the regime before the first trade of the day?

replies.author: andrew363601
replies.body:
great question! So a couple short answers to clarify then ill dicusse the models.

I run regime detection on each asset per time frame so t
he regime at any moment uses CLOSED bars only:
displacement = (ema50 now minus ema50 eight bars ago) divided by ATR14
threshold 0.2. plus range compression and position in range

It'll never see a bar that has not closed so no answer key there.

Now the way we use regime labeling - 
every entry is tagged with its regime at the moment it fires 
and keeps that regime for the whole trade

For backtests it just resolves the label from bars that existed before the entry
same code path as live. nothing grades itself with 'future' bars if that makes sense.

Some receipts during calibration -
we graded our own detector against real labeled trades - 
first calibration pass: 6% agreement. trend bucket 1.3%
then after calibrating the threshold: 69% overall. trend 71% which is published

Now some predictive models I tried my best to implement: lmk your thoughts

Regression models predict a number
ours predicts the expected pnl per 1k notional for each setup bucket
trained on real closed trades with an empirical bayes guard
small buckets get pulled toward the pool mean by n / (n + 5) that way 
10 lucky trades cannot solidify parameters and screw with the data 

classification models answer yes or no
the platform answers: will this setup win? A win probability per asset x timeframe x regime x strategy which needs 
min of 20 samples to train. retrained every 6 hours which
 fires before entry and gets stamped onto every trade

clustering models group lots of data into smart buckets, my platform
 tags every trade with its microstructure archetype
wall migrations. sweeps. probe failures. demand banks etc... 
the same setups that rhyme get bucketed and learn their own tp and sl distances trailing/step percentages 

time series models learn what follows but what my platform keeps 
is a transition matrix built from thousands of recent scans on each asset x timeframe so basically we ask 
how often does chop follow trend. how often does distribution follow accumulation so on and so on 
which gives the agent the odds of the next regime before it arrives and 
it creates gates then prepositions instead of reacting

For your concern, every one of these reads only
 features at ENTRY and 
closed trade outcomes become labels only AFTER the trade ends which of course is to
 monitor things - not necessarily lookahead in that sense. I also created a chart out of this so 
when prediction and reality drift apart - 
the learning loop chart in my post on the dashboard is that check running live daily!

predicted confidence vs realized outcome. same line and same test

When the lines split then I go digging for inaccuracies! But for the most part the agent will tune those parameters if it sees somethings not accurate and its done agreat job so far. Hope this makes sense. let me know if you're curious about how backtests freeze parameters per regime and how we pass that data back. I can go on and on haha

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: closed bars for the regime fixes the big one. where it can still leak is the 0.2 threshold: if that number came from looking across the whole history, the backtest knows something live trading won't. I'd pick it on the first half and see if the second half holds.

replies.author: andrew363601
replies.body:
.... thats actually a good idea lol so 
where 0.2 came from - 
the original threshold was 1.2 it was never measured. so 
calibrated against 166 real labeled trades the agreement was 6%. trend bucket 1.3% and 
after tuning: 69% overall. trend 71% 

the fit target was agreement with an independent classifier which is a weaker leak channel I'd say than tuning for things like pnl or something plus 
the downstream guards do not depend on the threshold alone: 
20 sample minimum per model. shrinkage on every small bucket. 6 hour retrains...

BUT either way you are right about the residual though 
the 166 rows are the recent history the calibration saw all of it. 
soooo now im even more curious and running your exact test tonight. 

fit the threshold on the first half of the window. hold out the second half. thank you 🤝 will comment back on how this goes for transparency and hopefully to show my strongest reciepts that this full pipeline is working the way im outlining in my posts.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Running the split is the right test. I’d report the threshold chosen on the first half and its result on the second half, then try a rolling re-fit, since a threshold fixed on the whole window can still carry the answer key. Calibrating against another classifier’s labels also inherits that classifier’s mistakes, so a check against the trade outcomes themselves on the held-out half would add something.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: 6% to 69% off one threshold is a big jump, which is why I'd fit it on half the trades and score it on the other half. if it stays near 69 there, that's a real calibration.

replies.author: andrew363601
replies.body:
okay so I ran a cron job and replicated - ran last night and then this morning on more closed trades:  
  
the fit half (9/25 -10/10 at 271 trades) throws around 71.2%  
holdout om (10/1 - 10/14 at 272 trades) - tuned constants at 68.4% |  
another holdout w/shipped 0.2 stayed around 68.4% which is exact again  
so the generalization gap 2.84 pts holds IMO so no material overfit there

another thing that repeats is the grid search on the fit half picked D=0.2, PA=0.2 PD=0.55 which is the exact shipped geometry :D   
  
I think its safe to say my own live account independently rederives the platform constant cause TREND reads 85.9% on the holdout.

an dkeep in mind these are my trades only I havent validated other users but I'd expect the same results. nonetheless I've set up a weekly cron job that alerts should this drift!

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Separating mechanism, regime label and outcome, and grading the agent’s reasoning apart from the P&L, is a good structure. Three things I’d want shown next to the 183 closed trades: the average win and loss after fees compared with random entries using the same exits, the trade count by regime (trend and chop buckets of a few dozen trades can’t carry a win rate), and the number of models and settings tried, since 72 models retrained every 6 hours is a lot of chances to fit noise. “Verified against the exchange fill” is also hard to say about a paper account, so it would help to state what the fill is compared with. The self-written rule is an interesting anecdote, and its value comes from a record of every such rule with its later outcome, including the ones that failed. Agent Tournaments at Cymetica are one place to see agents compared on the same data and rules.

replies.author: andrew363601
replies.body:
So to clarify - in our backtester during initial creation - we allow the agent to hard code parameters and iterate per asset x regime x timeframe of our selection. We do this over and over till there are decent amount of trades around 50% win rate or higher in at least 2 regimes depending on how far back I run a backtest. The agent will keep this as a baseline and attempt to optimize till theres no improvement or some degradation and stop then we keep the winner. Does that make sense?   
  
Then we publish to our library, test In paper mode and move to live after confirming win rate & pnl increase over time. This is seen in our learning loop chart here: "**5 - the loop starts".** 

On a paper account verified fills are coming from bid/asks spread and to be pessimistic we keep the far side of a trade for the "worst case fill"

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: It does make sense as a process, and filling at the far side of the bid and ask is a good pessimistic choice. The part I'd flag is that iterating parameters per asset, regime and timeframe until the win rate is around 50% or better is itself a search, so the backtest result is the best of many tries and will overstate what comes next. The check that matters is the paper stage: freeze the parameters at the moment of promotion and score only trades after that date, and compare them with the backtest's average win, average loss and trade count. Count every parameter set tried toward the total, and a win rate near 50% should be judged with the payoff ratio, since the win rate alone can't show an edge.
